routes.label: Split by the first coin flips

officialSolution.label: 2019 AMC 10A
officialSolution.sourceTerms: The linked source retains its printed copyright notice and host terms. This project adds no copy of this PDF.

question: Real numbers between \(0\) and \(1,\) inclusive, are chosen in the following manner. A fair coin is flipped. If it lands heads, then it is flipped again and the chosen number is \(0\) if the second flip is heads, and \(1\) if the second flip is tails. On the other hand, if the first coin flip is tails, then the number is chosen uniformly at random from the closed interval \([0,1].\) Two random numbers \(x\) and \(y\) are chosen independently in this manner. What is the probability that \(|x-y| > \tfrac{1}{2}?\)
solution:
Separate the possibilities according to the first coin flip for each number. A first flip of heads selects an endpoint, \(0\) or \(1\), with equal probability; tails selects a uniform number from \([0,1]\).

1. Both first flips are heads. This has probability \(\frac14\). The endpoint pairs \((0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\) are equally likely, and two have distance greater than \(\frac12\). This case contributes
\[
\frac14\cdot\frac12=\frac18.
\]

2. Exactly one first flip is heads. This has probability \(2\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac12\). If the endpoint is \(0\), the uniform number must exceed \(\frac12\); if the endpoint is \(1\), it must be less than \(\frac12\). Each event has probability \(\frac12\), so this case contributes
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac14.
\]

3. Both first flips are tails. This has probability \(\frac14\). Independence makes \((x,y)\) uniform in the unit square. The condition is
\[
y>x+\frac12
\quad\text{or}\quad
x>y+\frac12.
\]
These regions are two opposite corner triangles, each with perpendicular legs of length \(\frac12\). Their total area is
\[
2\left(\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12\right)=\frac14.
\]
The boundary lines have area zero, so the strict inequalities give the same area probability. This case contributes \(\frac14\cdot\frac14=\frac1{16}\).

The three cases are disjoint and exhaustive. Adding their contributions gives
\[
\frac18+\frac14+\frac1{16}
=\boxed{\frac7{16}},
\]
choice \(\textbf{B}\).
